title: Deprecate allow_no_jobs and allow_no_datafeeds in favor of allow_no_match

timeline.body:
This PR deprecates `allow_no_jobs` and `allow_no_datafeeds` API parameters in favor of `allow_no_match`.
The old parameters are still accepted by the APIs but the deprecation warning is emitted if the old parameter name is used in the request body or as a request param.

High-level REST client classes will now send the new `allow_no_match` parameter to the backend.

Closes #60642
Is there a "deprecation" field or something for these parameters? Clients generate their code from these specs and we probably don't want them generating with this parameter as an option.

reply.body: This comment goes for ALL the changed rest specs
If we don't want the clients to include this option we should just remove it from these specs.
Since most (if not all) clients are not BWC, it should probably be removed.

I decided to keep those deprecated params as without them yml tests do not work and I do see a value in keeping the yml tests for those params.
Added `deprecated` flag so that those params stand out.

timeline.body:
it seems to me that the default way to use these parameters via an API is through the request parameter (not in the body). 

Does this add a deprecation warning if the user provides `allow_no_jobs` as a URL param?

reply.body:
> it seems to me that the default way to use these parameters via an API is through the request parameter (not in the body).

That's correct. Some of the API methods do not even support body.

> Does this add a deprecation warning if the user provides allow_no_jobs as a URL param?

It did not add the warning. Now it does. Done.
